# voice-archive v2 — implementation spec

Three files are changed. **Each is owned by exactly one implementer. Do not edit
any file you do not own.** All three communicate only through the contracts
below, which are authoritative — if something is underspecified, follow the
letter of this document rather than inventing an alternative.

```
~/.pi/agent/extensions/voice-archive/index.ts     (owner: EXTENSION)
~/.pi/agent/extensions/voice-archive/server.mjs   (owner: SERVER)
~/.pi/agent/extensions/voice-archive/ui.html      (owner: UI)
```

Real path (edit here; `~/.pi/agent/extensions` is a symlink to it):
`/Users/michael.schmitt/projects/dotfiles/pi/.pi/agent/extensions/voice-archive/`

---

## 0. Background: what exists today (all verified working — do not regress it)

`pi-voice` (a third-party pi package) speaks a one-sentence summary of the
agent's reply after each response: an LLM rewrites the reply into ~22 spoken
words, a local Kokoro TTS server synthesizes it, `afplay` plays it, and the WAV
is deleted. It publishes two events on pi's shared extension event bus:

```
voice:speak_start { text, voice, speed, source }   // synthesis requested
voice:speak_end   { text, source, error? }         // playback finished/failed
```

`source` is `"auto"` (automatic after a response), `"tool"` (agent called the
`tts` tool), or `"sample"` (settings preview — always ignored by us).

Our extension listens to those events, re-requests the identical audio from the
same Kokoro server (`POST http://127.0.0.1:8181/tts`), transcodes it to Opus
with `ffmpeg`, and stores it. Storage is two immutable writes:

1. **Session log** — `pi.appendEntry("voice-note", {...})` writes one line into
   pi's own per-session JSONL (`~/.pi/agent/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<iso>_<uuid>.jsonl`).
   Written synchronously during `voice:speak_start`, because by the time
   archival synthesis finishes pi may have torn the session down. Holds **facts
   only**:
   ```json
   {"v":1,"noteId":"2026-08-05T16-53-24-308Z-000","sessionId":"019f…","ts":"2026-08-05T16:53:24.308Z",
    "text":"Still on it.","voice":"af_heart","speed":1.25,"source":"auto"}
   ```
2. **Archive** — `~/.pi/voice-archive/<session-id>/<noteId>.opus` plus a
   self-describing `<noteId>.json` sidecar holding the **derived** facts
   (`audio`, `bytes`, `durationMs`, `cwd`, optional `error`). Written after
   synthesis resolves.

`noteId` joins the two. The server reads both and folds in "archive-only" notes
(whose `appendEntry` failed, e.g. in headless `pi -p` runs where the session is
gone before pi-voice even finishes summarizing) so nothing is ever invisible.

Existing server routes (all must keep working):

```
GET  /                      ui.html
GET  /api/health            { ok, archiveDir, tts }
GET  /api/sessions[?voice=1]  session summaries, newest first
GET  /api/session/:id       { meta, items } chronological timeline
GET  /api/audio/<relpath>   archived audio (path-traversal guarded → 403)
POST /api/tts               { text, voice?, speed? } → WAV, live synthesis
```

Timeline `items` are `{kind:"user"|"assistant"|"voice", id, ts, text, ...}`
sorted by `ts`. Assistant items carry `tools:[{name,args}]`, `model`,
`hasThinking`. Voice items carry `noteId, voice, speed, source, audio,
durationMs, bytes, error, orphan?`.

Constraints that shaped all of this and still hold:
- Single user, localhost only, no auth, no build step, **zero npm dependencies**
  in `server.mjs` and `ui.html`. `index.ts` may only import from `node:*` and
  `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (type-only).
- Never couple to pi-voice internals (its temp dir, filenames, private
  functions). Only its documented events and HTTP API.
- The server is read-only with respect to pi's session files. It must never
  write into `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.

---

## 1. Feature: live per-session processing status

The user wants to *see*, per active session, that it is currently turning a
response into a voice note, and which stage it is in.

Two pi processes can run concurrently, and the UI server is a **separate
process**, so status is exchanged through files.

### Status file (written by EXTENSION, read by SERVER)

Path: `~/.pi/voice-archive/status/<session-id>.json`
Write atomically (write `<file>.tmp` then `rename`) on every phase change.

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "sessionId": "019fd2d8-0965-784d-aaff-40d938ee1c8a",
  "pid": 51234,
  "cwd": "/Users/michael.schmitt/projects/demo",
  "phase": "idle",
  "detail": "",
  "queueDepth": 0,
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-05T17:10:00.000Z"
}
```

`phase` is exactly one of:

| phase | meaning | set when |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | nothing in flight | session start; after the last work drains |
| `summarizing` | an LLM is turning a response into the spoken sentence | we expect pi-voice to summarize, or our own auto-queue starts an LLM call |
| `speaking` | Kokoro is synthesizing / `afplay` is playing it aloud | `voice:speak_start` |
| `archiving` | we are re-synthesizing + transcoding for the archive | our archive job starts |

`detail` is a short human string (≤80 chars), e.g. the note text being worked
on, or `"auto-queue 2/3"`. `queueDepth` is the number of pending archive jobs.

EXTENSION must delete the status file on `session_shutdown`.

### Staleness (SERVER)

A pi process can crash mid-phase and leave a stale file. The server treats a
status as **dead** and ignores it if either:
- the pid is gone — `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws `ESRCH`, or
- `updatedAt` is older than 15 minutes.

A status that is alive but whose `phase !== "idle"` and whose `updatedAt` is
older than 3 minutes is reported with `stalled: true` (the UI greys it out)
rather than being hidden — a wedged ollama call should be visible, not silently
dropped.

### Route (SERVER)

```
GET /api/status  →  { sessions: { "<session-id>": { phase, detail, queueDepth, pid, cwd, updatedAt, stalled } } }
```
Only live entries. Cheap enough to poll every second; do not cache.

### UI

- Poll `GET /api/status` every **1000 ms**.
- In the sidebar, a session that has a live status shows an animated indicator:
  a pulsing dot plus a short label (`summarizing`, `speaking`, `archiving`).

  cache it for the process lifetime). Missing file / entry ⇒ disabled.
- Collect candidates on `pi.on("turn_end", …)`: `event.message` is that turn's
  assistant message. Record `{ entryId, text }` where `text` is its concatenated
  `text` content blocks. Skip messages with no text (pure tool-call turns).
  - Get `entryId` by matching the message against the tail of
    `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` (last assistant message entry). If it
    cannot be resolved, still queue the note with `sourceEntryId: null`.
- Process the collected batch on `pi.on("agent_end", …)`, **after** the normal
  `pendingSource` capture:
  - **Drop the final collected message if pi-voice will already voice it** —
    i.e. when voice config `enabled !== false` and `events.agent_end` exists.
    Otherwise keep it. This is the whole dedup story; without it every response
    gets two near-identical notes.
  - Clear the batch afterwards, always, including on error.
- For each remaining message, in order, serially:
  1. Generate the spoken sentence with an LLM, reusing the user's own tuned
     prompt and model from `~/.pi/voice/config.json` → `events.agent_end.prompt`
     and `events.agent_end.model` (fall back to the active session model). If
     there is no such prompt, skip auto-queue entirely.
  2. Synthesize via `POST /tts`, transcode to Opus, and store it through the
     **existing** archive path, with `source: "queue"` and the correct
     `sourceEntryId` / `sourceText`.
  3. Append the session-log entry too, via the same `appendEntry` call the
     normal path uses (tolerating the stale-session failure the same way).

  audio queue or `afplay`. The user is not listening to a backlog; they are
  browsing it later.
- Keep it strictly serial and behind the existing archive chain, so we never run
  two ollama calls or two Kokoro requests at once. Update the status file with
  phase `summarizing` / `archiving` and `detail` like `"auto-queue 2/3"`.

For the LLM call, copy the approach pi-voice itself uses (it is the only
supported way to run a one-off side session, and it deliberately loads no
extensions/skills so it cannot recurse into voice handling). Reference
implementation, verbatim from
`~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/@s1m0n38/pi-voice/extensions/index.ts`:

```typescript
import { createAgentSession, DefaultResourceLoader, ModelRuntime, SessionManager } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";

let runtimePromise: Promise<ModelRuntime> | undefined;
function getModelRuntime(): Promise<ModelRuntime> {
  runtimePromise ??= ModelRuntime.create();
  return runtimePromise;
}

async function generateSpeechText(prompt, context, ctx, modelConfig) {
  const model = modelConfig ? ctx.modelRegistry.find(modelConfig.provider, modelConfig.id) : ctx.model;
  if (!model) return null;
  const userMessage = `The following is a message from a conversation that you need to summarize:\n\n""""\n${context}\n""""`;
  const loader = new DefaultResourceLoader({
    cwd: process.cwd(),
    agentDir: resolve(homedir(), ".pi", "agent"),
    systemPromptOverride: () => prompt,
    noExtensions: true, noSkills: true, noPromptTemplates: true, noThemes: true, noContextFiles: true,
  });
  await loader.reload();
  const { session } = await createAgentSession({
    model, tools: [],
    sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(),
    modelRuntime: await getModelRuntime(),
    resourceLoader: loader,
  });
  try {
    let responseText = "";
    const unsub = session.subscribe((event) => {
      if (event.type === "message_end" && event.message.role === "assistant") {
        for (const part of event.message.content) if (part.type === "text" && part.text) responseText += part.text;
      }
    });
    await session.prompt(userMessage);
    unsub();
    return responseText || null;
  } finally {
    session.dispose();
  }
}
```

`ctx.modelRegistry`). Auto-queue runs during `agent_end`, while the session is
alive, so capture the `ctx` handed to that handler and use it for that batch
only — never store it across events (it goes stale and throws).

The UI exposes `autoQueue` as a per-session toggle (a switch in the session
header) with a tooltip explaining that it summarizes and archives every

sessions that are currently live, so also surface it there; for a dead session
